encounters.name: A Familiar Voice
encounters.description: Your comms crackle with an encrypted hail. The voice on the other end is unmistakable: Captain Reva Sato of the Guild escort Heron. 'I've been hoping to run into you again, Captain. I've been doing some digging since you pulled me out of that wreck. Those raiders who hit my convoy? They were using mil-spec targeting systems. Hardware that doesn't leave Guild armories without authorization codes. Someone inside the Guild set us up.'

choices.label: Ask for Specifics
choices.description: Push Sato for names, serial numbers, anything concrete.

outcome.description: Sato transmits a data packet: weapons serial numbers traced to a Guild depot on Kessler Station, signed out under a name that doesn't appear in any personnel roster. 'Ghost requisitions,' she calls them. 'Whoever is running this operation has access to the highest clearance levels. Watch your back, Captain. I'll keep digging from my end.'

choices.label: Warn Her to Stay Safe
choices.description: Tell Sato to be careful.

outcome.description: Sato laughs, but there's an edge to it. 'I survived the wreck. I'll survive the politics.' She sends you a set of comm frequencies used by the raider ships, scavenged from her Heron's damaged flight recorder. 'Keep your ears open. These frequencies are still active.'

choices.label: Stay Out of It
choices.description: Wish her well and cut the channel.

outcome.description: Sato's voice goes flat. 'Understood, Captain. I won't forget what you did for me, but I get it. Not everyone wants to poke the hive.' The channel closes.

encounters.name: The Heron's Shadow
encounters.description: Your sensors register a contact: a ship signature that matches the Guild escort Heron, Captain Sato's vessel. The one you left drifting when you ignored her distress call. The contact holds position for three seconds, then vanishes from your display. It leaves no debris field or ion trail. Just empty space where a dead ship shouldn't be.

choices.label: Investigate the Contact
choices.description: Divert to the last known coordinates.

outcome.description: You sweep the area with every sensor you have. The results come back empty. But your nav computer logs one detail: the ghost contact was broadcasting a Guild transponder code that was decommissioned two weeks ago. Sato's code.

choices.label: Run Sensor Diagnostics
choices.description: Check your instruments.

outcome.description: Your diagnostics come back clean: every system nominal. The contact was real, or at least your sensors believed it was. You log the anomaly and file it with the growing list of things that don't add up.

choices.label: Keep Flying
choices.description: Adjust course and keep flying.

outcome.description: You adjust course. The sensor ghost fades behind you, just like the distress signal did.

encounters.name: Encrypted Channel: Torres
encounters.description: An encrypted burst transmission hits your comm array, routed through six relay stations and a Crimson Reach dead drop. The decryption key matches one Malia Torres gave you. The message is terse: 'Captain. Weapons moving through Reach space. Not ours. Too clean, too expensive. Guild markings filed off but the alloy composition is unmistakable. Someone is arming the frontier and making it look like pirate procurement. Attached coordinates of the next scheduled drop. Wrench'

choices.label: Investigate the Drop Coordinates
choices.description: Head to the coordinates Torres provided. See who's making the delivery.

outcome.description: You arrive early and run silent. A Guild-registered cargo hauler drops three sealed containers at the coordinates, then jumps out without logging the stop. The containers' manifests are blank, but your scans detect military-grade pulse cannons and targeting arrays inside. You photograph everything and transmit the evidence to Torres. Her reply is a single word: 'Deeper.'

choices.label: Forward to Authorities
choices.description: Send the coordinates to Frontier Alliance patrols. Let them handle it.

outcome.description: You relay Torres' intel to the nearest Alliance patrol. They promise to investigate. A day later, Torres sends another message: 'Patrol arrived. Drop site was clean. They knew. Someone tipped them off.'

choices.label: Delete the Message
choices.description: Purge the transmission and the decryption key.

outcome.description: You wipe the decryption key and purge the comm logs. As you clear the buffers, a secondary header on the message shows someone else intercepted it before it reached you.

encounters.name: The Nervous Courier
encounters.description: A Guild-registered light freighter drops out of transit on an intercept course. No weapons lock or hostile posture, just a frantic hail on an open channel. The pilot's face appears on your display: young, sweating, eyes darting. 'You're the one asking questions about the arms shipments, right? I have something. A manifest. The real one, not the sanitized version they file with customs. I need to hand it off before they realize it's missing. Please. I don't have much time.'

choices.label: Accept the Manifest
choices.description: Dock with the courier and take the data.

outcome.description: The docking sequence takes forty seconds. The courier's hands shake as they transfer a sealed data chip. The manifest lists weapons shipments across eight systems: quantities, dates, and authorization codes that trace back to a Guild department that officially doesn't exist. 'They call themselves The Ledger,' the courier whispers. 'That's all I know. Please. Don't let this disappear.' The freighter undocks and jumps before you can respond.

choices.label: Demand Verification
choices.description: Make them prove the data is legitimate before you touch it.

outcome.description: The courier transmits a sample: three entries from the manifest with verifiable details. You cross-reference against public shipping records. The official logs show agricultural supplies. The manifest shows pulse rifles and shield generators. The discrepancy is undeniable. You accept the full data chip, but the delay costs precious minutes. The courier's ship departs at maximum burn, and you catch a brief sensor flash: another vessel was watching from the debris field nearby.

choices.label: Refuse the Handoff
choices.description: Turn the courier away.

outcome.description: The courier stares at you through the display, desperation collapsing into defeat. 'Then it dies with me,' they say quietly. The freighter peels away and vanishes into transit. You never learn the courier's name. A week later, a Guild bulletin reports a light freighter lost to 'engine malfunction' in deep space. No survivors recovered.

encounters.name: Off the Books
encounters.description: A tight-beam transmission punches through your comm filters. No sender ID or routing header, just raw encrypted audio. The diction is clipped and precise: Officer Larsen, Guild Security. 'Listen carefully. I'm using a personal encryption key, so we have maybe ninety seconds before their monitoring sweeps catch this. Your ship has been flagged for extended customs inspection at every Guild-controlled station. That's not standard procedure. That's surveillance. Someone with authority is tracking your movements and cargo. I can't tell you who. I can't tell you why. But I can tell you to vary your routes and avoid Guild docking priority lanes for the next few weeks. Larsen out.'

choices.label: Heed the Warning
choices.description: Take Larsen's advice. Adjust your routes and stay off Guild radar.

outcome.description: You reprogram your nav computer to favor secondary lanes and independent stations. It adds time to every journey. Over the next few days, Guild patrol ships linger in systems you would have passed through on your old routes.

choices.label: Try to Trace the Order
choices.description: Search the Guild customs databases for the order that flagged your ship.

outcome.description: You spend hours digging through publicly accessible Guild customs databases, cross-referencing your ship's ID against inspection logs. The pattern is clear: every station you've docked at in the last month has queued an 'enhanced review' of your cargo within hours of your departure. The authorization codes all route back to a single internal department: Commerce Oversight Division, Section Nine. A department with no public charter and no listed personnel.

choices.label: Ignore the Warning
choices.description: Keep your regular routes. Business as usual.

outcome.description: You maintain your regular routes. Nothing changes immediately, but a week later your customs clearance times have tripled. Inspectors are pulling apart your cargo bay with unusual thoroughness.

encounters.name: Military-Grade Wreckage
encounters.description: Your sensors flag a debris field ahead: the remains of a pirate raider, torn apart by what looks like its own weapons overload. As you drift closer, the wreckage tells its story. The hull is standard pirate retrofit, but the weapons mounted on it are anything but: military-grade pulse arrays, factory-sealed targeting computers, and a shield generator that belongs on a Guild cruiser, not a raider skiff.

choices.label: Salvage the Weapons Data
choices.description: Pull the serial numbers and targeting logs from the wreckage.

outcome.description: You spend an hour in the debris field, extracting data cores and photographing serial plates. Every weapon traces back to Guild military contracts: hardware that was officially destroyed or reported lost in transit. The targeting computer's last calibration was performed at a Guild enforcement yard.

choices.label: Strip Usable Components
choices.description: Take what you can carry.

outcome.description: You pull two intact pulse arrays and a functioning shield capacitor from the wreck. As you load the last piece, your scanner catches something etched into the capacitor housing: a Guild logistics stamp, half-scraped away.

choices.label: Log Coordinates and Leave
choices.description: Tag the wreck for authorities and move on.

outcome.description: You drop a nav beacon and transmit the coordinates to the nearest patrol frequency. As you pull away, the wreck tumbles slowly into the asteroid field.

encounters.name: The Shadow on Your Six
encounters.description: For the last three jumps, the same sensor contact has held at the edge of detection range, always matching your course changes with a thirty-second delay. An unmarked vessel, running with minimal emissions. On the third jump, they finally hail. No video. Synthesized voice. 'We know what you've found. We know who you've spoken to. This is your opportunity to walk away with your ship and your life intact.'

choices.label: Defy the Threat
choices.description: Open a channel and answer them.

outcome.description: You broadcast on the same frequency: 'I've backed up everything I know to three separate locations. Anything happens to me, it goes public.' Silence. Then a single ping. The shadow vessel's engines flare and it breaks off pursuit, jumping to transit.

choices.label: Try to Identify the Ship
choices.description: Run every scan you have on the shadow vessel.

outcome.description: Your sensors strain against the vessel's emission dampeners, but you manage to pull a partial hull signature. The alloy composition matches Guild military construction: not a converted freighter, but a purpose-built surveillance ship. You store the signature data alongside your growing evidence file.

choices.label: Go Dark for a While
choices.description: Lose yourself in commercial traffic and stick to routine runs.

outcome.description: You alter course to a busy trade lane and lose yourself in commercial traffic. The shadow vessel doesn't follow. Or at least, you can't detect it anymore. For the next few days, you stick to routine trading runs and keep your head down. But the data you've collected doesn't delete itself.

encounters.name: The Pulse Deepens
encounters.description: Your sensors are screaming. The energy phenomenon you scanned before has changed. Dramatically. What was once a swirling curiosity has expanded into a structured pattern, pulsing in intervals that your nav computer insists are non-random. The charged particles are arranging themselves into geometric formations, and the energy output has increased tenfold. Research buoys in the area have gone silent. Your instruments are detecting something impossible: the phenomenon is responding to your approach.

choices.label: Conduct a Full Spectrum Analysis
choices.description: Push your sensors to their limits.

outcome.description: Your instruments record data. The pulse pattern resolves into a repeating mathematical sequence, neither natural nor random. Encoded within it, your computer isolates what appear to be navigational coordinates, pointing to a region of space that appears on no chart in your nav database. Then, as suddenly as it started, the phenomenon contracts to a point of light and goes still. Your sensor logs are the only proof it was ever there.

choices.label: Move Closer
choices.description: Edge into the outer boundary of the phenomenon.

outcome.description: You edge your ship into the outer boundary of the phenomenon. Your hull vibrates at a frequency that rattles in your teeth. The pulse pattern shifts (faster, more complex) and your nav computer begins receiving data it can't parse. Raw information, flooding your systems. You pull back before the input overwhelms your processors, but the fragment you captured contains coordinates and what might be a timestamp.

choices.label: Withdraw to Safe Distance
choices.description: Reverse thrust and put fifty kilometers between you and it.

outcome.description: You reverse thrust and put fifty kilometers between you and the phenomenon. From this distance, you watch it pulse and shift for another hour before it settles into a slow, rhythmic glow. Your sensors record the pattern. Whatever it is, it seems content to wait. You file the observation and mark the coordinates.

encounters.name: A Friend in Low Places
encounters.description: A familiar comm signature pings your ship: one of your black market contacts, using the encrypted channel reserved for time-sensitive opportunities. But this isn't a sales pitch. 'Captain, I've got something that's worth more than cargo. You've been asking about that shadow operation. The Ledger? My people move goods through every station in the Expanse. We see things. I've put together a shipping pattern (dates, routes, volumes) that shows exactly how they're moving weapons through legitimate Guild supply chains. It's yours, but information this dangerous isn't free.'

choices.label: Pay for the Data
choices.description: Transfer the credits.

outcome.description: The data arrives in a compressed burst: months of shipping records, cross-referenced with Guild manifests and black market movement logs. The pattern is damning: every major weapons shipment to pirate groups in the last year was routed through three specific Guild logistics hubs, all managed by the same administrative department. Section Nine. The name keeps surfacing. Your contact adds a personal note: 'Burn this after you read it. These people make pirates look civilized.'

choices.label: Trade Information Instead
choices.description: Offer what you already know about The Ledger in exchange. Knowledge for knowledge.

outcome.description: Your contact considers the offer, then agrees. You share the weapons serial data and courier manifest; they send you their shipping analysis. The combined intelligence paints a picture of an operation far larger than a few corrupt officials: The Ledger has been running parallel supply chains across the entire Expanse for years. Your contact's parting words: 'We're both targets now. At least we're informed targets.'

choices.label: Decline the Offer
choices.description: Decline the offer.

outcome.description: Your contact shrugs over the comm. 'Your call, Captain. But this data has a shelf life. Once they rotate their routes, and they will, it's worthless.' The channel closes.

encounters.name: Displaced Voices
encounters.description: A cluster of civilian transports drifts at the edge of a transit lane, overcrowded, under-fueled, broadcasting a general assistance request. When you hail the lead ship, the captain identifies them as settlers from Voss Station, a mining outpost. 'The Guild called it a relocation program. Said the station needed structural repairs and we'd be back in six months. That was a year ago. They sealed the docking bays and told us to find new berths elsewhere. Without compensation. Without a timeline. We've heard the same story from three other stations.'

choices.label: Record Their Testimony
choices.description: Get names, dates, and details on the record.

outcome.description: You spend two hours conducting interviews across three ships. The stories are consistent and damning: Guild officials arriving with armed escorts, forty-eight-hour eviction notices, sealed habitation decks converted to something. The settlers don't know what. But one former dock worker describes cargo containers being loaded into the sealed sections: unmarked, heavy, and escorted by personnel wearing no insignia. You transmit fuel reserves and ration packs, and add twenty-seven sworn testimonies to your evidence file.

choices.label: Provide Supplies
choices.description: Transfer fuel cells, water cartridges, and rations.

outcome.description: You dock with the lead transport and transfer what you can spare: fuel cells, water recycler cartridges, two weeks of rations. The settlers' gratitude is quiet and heavy. As you prepare to undock, a former dock worker pulls you aside. 'I took pictures,' she says. 'Of the cargo they brought in after they kicked us out. I'll transmit them to your ship. Someone should see this.' The images show crates stamped with a stylized ledger book.

choices.label: Wish Them Well
choices.description: Point them to the nearest independent station.

outcome.description: You transmit the coordinates of the nearest independent station and wish them safe travels. The convoy drifts on. You log Voss Station.

encounters.name: Last Warning
encounters.description: Every screen on your bridge goes dark. Then, one by one, they flicker back to life displaying the same message in stark white text against black: 'STOP DIGGING. LAST WARNING.' The transmission source is untraceable: routed through your own ship's internal comm system, which means someone has penetrated your security protocols. As you scramble to purge the intrusion, a final line appears: 'Everyone you've spoken to. Everything you've collected. We have it all. Walk away, or we dismantle everything you've built. Starting with the people who helped you.'

choices.label: Distribute Your Evidence
choices.description: Send copies of everything to every contact you have.

outcome.description: You spend the next hour transmitting encrypted copies of every document and scan you've collected to every trusted contact in your network. Torres. Larsen. Your black market connections. Independent media outlets on three stations. The screens return to normal, and your security sweep finds and purges the intrusion code.

choices.label: Trace the Intrusion
choices.description: Let the intrusion code run and trace its pathway.

outcome.description: You let the intrusion code run while your secondary systems map its communication pathway. The trace leads through fourteen relay points before terminating at a Guild communications satellite in high orbit above Kessler Station, the same station linked to the ghost weapons requisitions. The satellite's access logs show it's been used for hundreds of similar untraceable transmissions over the past two years. You've found The Ledger's comm backbone.

choices.label: Consider Their Terms
choices.description: Stop reaching out.

outcome.description: You sit in the dark bridge for a long time, staring at the fading text. You don't delete your files, but you stop reaching out. You stop asking questions. The screens clear, your systems normalize, and the void outside your viewport looks exactly as empty as it always does.

encounters.name: Convergence
encounters.description: Three transmissions arrive within an hour of each other: different encryption, different routing, different voices, but the same urgency. Your contacts across the Expanse have been working independently, and they've all reached the same conclusion at the same time. One by one, they patch into a shared encrypted channel. For the first time, the people you've brought into this web can hear each other.

choices.label: Coordinate a Joint Operation
choices.description: Everyone brings their piece. Together, you plan the next move.

outcome.description: The channel comes alive. Each contact contributes their fragment: shipping routes, weapons data, financial records, refugee testimonies, comm intercepts. Assembled together, the evidence describes a conspiracy that has infiltrated every level of Guild governance. The Ledger isn't a rogue department. It's a parallel power structure that has been steering the Commerce Guild for over a decade. The channel goes quiet. Then someone says: 'So. How do we tear it down?'

choices.label: Release Everything to the Public
choices.description: No more secrets. Broadcast the evidence on every open channel in the Expanse.

outcome.description: You compile every shred of evidence into a single data package and broadcast it across civilian, military, and independent news frequencies simultaneously. Within hours, the Expanse is in uproar. Guild officials scramble to respond. Frontier Alliance representatives demand emergency sessions. The Miners' Union calls for a full audit of Guild logistics. The Ledger's carefully maintained shadows are flooded with light. It's messy, chaotic, and uncontrollable.

choices.label: Hold the Evidence in Reserve
choices.description: Keep the evidence encrypted and distributed.

outcome.description: You convince your contacts to hold. The evidence stays encrypted, distributed, and ready. The channel signs off on one agreement: when the time comes, you move together. Not before.
